analysis: The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 4071-4930). The PR's changed ranges are mostly elsewhere in the file: head 3, 985-989, 3532-3540, 5234-5239 and later. None of the changes in the patch excerpt falls inside these units, so they are context only. The patch excerpt is truncated; it shows only documentation edits: the date bump, KV-slot re-slice floor text, and the cluster service health file note (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE, service-health.json versus part-health.json). The excerpt is documentation-only, so it adds no code, control, or authorization change. The examined base text covers cluster SSD prefix record encoding, load-agreement binding of the encoding, fail-closed refusal on mismatched precisions, and the sealed record header. That text relates to T-041 (the at-rest prefix artifact). It describes encryption, HMAC-named directories, and deletion of foreign-encoding or undecodable records, and it states that the changes do not weaken those mechanisms. The remaining sections (GPT-OSS paged KV, batch drivers, MiMo, Gemma, manifest pins, media transport) are descriptive and make qualification caveats explicit. They assert no new production activation. The one security-relevant claim is that manifest repair replaces manifest.json only when the fetched bytes match the same artifact identity (ClusterCatalogArtifact.sameArtifact). That is a pre-existing control and is unchanged here. Remaining uncertainty: the full patch (head lines 3532-3540, 5234-5288, 5295-5298, 5374-5376) is outside these units. A later pass should check it for claims that weaken the stated trust boundaries. In particular it should check the health-file handoff, where a supervisor liveness guard accepts only the service's own PID. The environment-variable separation is a documentation claim whose implementation was not supplied. No regression is identified in the supplied units.
